title: A naturally bound wild actor uses the current owner context

verification.actor: A real visible WILD Rattata from the raw-save field; exact handle, subject and current engine membership are required. Owner map-generation equality is measured, not used to hide acquisition failures.
verification.trigger: Boot the raw save normally and observe native public getContext returns during natural Wild activity.
verification.observable: The selected actor map generation equals the owner context on the same native public-return boundary. One subsequent actual Walk terminal trace supplies structured actor evidence, not a broad movement claim.

setupMutations.change: Import a disposable copy of test.sav with normal boot input; source ROM and save stay unchanged. After the completed record-start boundary, enable a read-only public-return hook. Observe one exact naturally present Wild actor, including one already present after boot; do not force a replacement or filter on matching owner generations.

limits: Shared actor.binding-current-context retains the original exact identity measurements. Host reader controls use the real callback with wrong register/context data; they are not live game fault injection.
Proves one natural Wild binding and one terminal motion. Does not prove all transitions, follower or mount setup, movement feel or long-run stability.
After boot, stop within 900 completed game frames or 4096 native cycles. A missing subject is a distinct failure, never a pass.

events.value: Boot the raw save with no actor or profile changes
Acquire a real visible Wild Rattata and compare its context with a real public getContext return
Observe one complete natural Walk for the same subject

stop.condition: Fail at the first owner-context mismatch, or stop after one same-subject terminal Walk; post-boot observation is capped at 900 game frames and 4096 native cycles

invariants: Each accepted motion has exactly one terminal result
Control returns after the selected motion finishes or cancels
Every active actor handle uses the current field epoch
